title.narrative: Unicef lot 11: project in Unity state - Rubkona, Guit, Mayom, Pariang and Abiemnon counties

description.narrative: Number and type(s) of direct beneficiaries 155,575 (F-80,889,M-74,676) Number and type(s) of indirect beneficiaries 311,150(F-161,7981,M-149,352)

South Sudan’s health system continues to suffer the effects of decades of conflict, and recurrent effects of poor weather while Covid 19 pandemic has stretched it further. Structures are weakened including leadership and governance, health care financing, commodities and supplies, human resources for health, service delivery, and health information systems. Even where health facilities are available, access and utilization are also not optimal given the many demand side barriers including weak community structures, poor access especially during the rainy seasons, insecurity, poverty and negative social cultural factors. Given this scenario, South Sudan has one of the worst health indicators globally. The country has a maternal mortality ratio of 1150 per 100,000 live births, and an equally high neonatal and under five mortality rates at 38.6 and 96.2 per 1000 respectively. There is low health service utilization rate at 0.60 per capita and poor coverage of critical services including childhood immunization (pentavalent 3 at 33%) and facility-based deliveries (19.4%). .

The objective of this project is to deliver live saving, low cost, high impact essential health services in Abiemnon, Guit, Mayom, Pariang and Rubkona counties and will target a catchment population of 597,512 inhabitants utilizing the health systems approach whereby the county health departments of Abiemnom, Guit, Mayom, Pariang and Rubkona counties will be supported to offer basic health services at the state, county, facility and community level.

description.narrative: The integration of climate risks in programming includes an undertaking of concrete actions to reduce and/or mitigate risks related to climate change impact and disaster risks ( for example droughts, erosion, salinization, flooding, etc.) The projects we refer to could be on the themes of health education, justice, security, disaster management, finance and livelihoods.
